text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: sudden spike in GPU driver resets on cluster 'inference-prod-3' (nv-host-reset / Xid=86) across nodes nv-13, nv-17, nv-22. Error rate up 18% in the last 2m.

incident-bot: Paging oncall @oncall-jordan (severity: P1) — https://ops.redwood/alerts/4182001234 : :rotating_light:

oncall-jordan: I’m awake, taking it. Initial check: k8s shows repeated OOMKill + container restart loops for runner pods pinned to nv-13 and nv-17. nvidia-smi on nv-13 shows ECC correctable errors ramping.

sre-mira: On nv-17 as well, dmesg shows a sequence of "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:05:00): 86" followed by firmware reset. Looks like driver resets correlating with memory errors (ECC).

infra-ops: Running quick health check across the fleet. Telemetry shows 4 nodes with rising correctable ECC counts and 2 nodes with uncorrectable increments. We'll hunt for pattern.

oncall-jordan: Immediate mitigation proposal: cordon + drain nv-13 and nv-17, move inference traffic off those nodes to avoid client 5xx. Can we do controlled drain?

eng-runtime: Agree. Also enable model-fallback routing for high-QPS routes so they hit the dedicated pool rather than opportunistic shared nodes. We can flip routing in the console to route by node-tag = dedicated-fast for the affected routes.

support-lee: Tier-1: We already have two customer reports of elevated 5xx on chat endpoints, one enterprise customer seeing ~20% error rate on inference calls. Notified cust-ops.

cust-ops: Preparing a customer message: status page draft ready once we confirm mitigation path. Recommend note: "We are routing traffic away from impacted GPU hosts and performing targeted reboots; some transients may be observed."

oncall-jordan: Executing cordon/drain now. Command:```bash
kubectl cordon nv-13 && kubectl drain nv-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -o yaml
kubectl cordon nv-17 && kubectl drain nv-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -o yaml
```

monitoring-bot: Noted: cordon/drain triggered for nv-13, nv-17. Autoscaler: launching replacement nodes in the pool to compensate for capacity.

sre-mira: While draining, we should collect kernel logs and GPU ECC counters. Commands:```bash
ssh root@nv-13 'dmesg | tail -n 200' > nv-13-dmesg.log
ssh root@nv-13 'nvidia-smi -q -d ECC' > nv-13-ecc.log
```

infra-ops: Collected logs and uploaded to /artifacts/incidents/4182001234/. Quick grep shows repeated patterns: "GPU at 0000:05:00: GPU has fallen off the bus" then Xid=86 resets.

eng-runtime: Workaround suggestion: temporarily disable persistent-volumes that keep large KV caches on these hosts to reduce memory pressure, and enable reduced batch sizes for in-flight requests. Update routing to add 5% sampling to fallback model to check quality.

oncall-jordan: Applying runtime throttle for heavy batch routes: adjusted batch_size limit from 64 -> 24 for route /v1/generate/high-qps. Pushing config:```json
{"route":"/v1/generate/high-qps","batch_size":24}
```

incident-bot: Incident timeline updated. Current status: Mitigation in progress. Impact: elevated 5xx and tail latency for some customers.

duty-lead-paul: Good call on draining. Next: can we attempt a driver restart once the node is drained and idle? If ECC counts continue rising, I favor taking nodes out of rotation and reprovisioning NIC/driver/kernel.

infra-ops: After drain, we ran:```bash
systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service || journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200
``` Driver restart logs show transient success but ECC counts persist. We'll reprovision node image for nv-17 and mark nv-13 for hardware debug.

eng-runtime: We should also flip fallback policies so that when a model instance fails with Xid driver reset we automatically retry on different pool rather than returning error to user. Patch ready: add retry on nvidia-reset error code with exponential backoff.

support-lee: Customer impacted list: acct-77 (enterprise), acct-112 (start-up), a handful of self-serve. Sending interim update: "We are routing traffic to alternate capacity and performing targeted host maintenance. Some requests may be retried or delayed."

cust-ops: Status page updated and sent to customers. No QBR-level impact expected, we will follow up if node hardware replacement is required.

oncall-jordan: Quick post-drain checks: nv-13 shows ongoing correctable ECC increase, marking NV-13 as suspect hardware. nv-17 reprovisioned, rejoined cluster, monitoring telemetry shows stable for now.

sre-mira: Action items for postmortem: capture time-series of ECC counters, list models affected, correlate per-route 5xx spikes, attach kernel/nvidia logs. Also run long-running burn-in on reprovisioned nodes to validate fix.

duty-lead-paul: I want a follow-up hardware ticket for nv-13 to the datacenter ops team: run memory scrub and do thermal/PSU checks. Assign to infra-hardware with priority high.

infra-ops: Created ticket INFRA-8732: "nv-13 suspected ECC hardware fault — run memtest, replace DIMM if needed" and linked to incident.

sre-mira: Note for post-incident controls: add a guard to routing to avoid scheduling latency-sensitive pods onto nodes with rising ECC correctable counters > threshold (currently 500). Also add a Grafana alarm to surface deltas over 5m windows.

eng-runtime: Small follow-up: we pushed the runtime retry patch to canary; it will retry failed inferences once on alternate pool to reduce immediate 5xx. Monitor for regressions.

oncall-jordan: Current status: nv-13 out of rotation pending hardware swap; nv-17 healthy after reprovision; overall 5xx rate dropping from peak 18% -> 3% in last 10m. Marking incident as mitigated but keeping channel open for handoff.

incident-bot: Oncall handoff scheduled in 25m to @sre-mira for night coverage with severity reduced to P2.

support-lee: Customer follow-up message drafted for tomorrow with technical summary and mitigation steps.

duty-lead-paul: Thanks team. Postmortem owners: sre-mira (lead), infra-ops (hardware investigation), eng-runtime (routing/retry changes). Please create the draft postmortem within 48h and include mitigation timeline and follow-up action owners. :memo:

sre-mira: Will do. Uploading collected artifacts and initial timeline to the postmortem doc.

oncall-jordan: Closing my active page, handing to @sre-mira for follow-up. If we see recurrence, escalate to datacenter on-call and consider temporarily moving affected queues to Dedicated capacity until fleet fix is in.

monitoring-bot: Alert cleared for Xid surge on inference-prod-3 at 4182001448.

incident-bot: Incident channel will remain open for 2 hours for monitoring, then archived if stable.
